intro.title: Daily resilience and balance check
intro.body: A short space to see how you're doing with pressure, tiredness, and energy — in plain language, without heavy labels. Choose where you are now, answer honestly, and get small insights you can use today. Everything stays in your browser.

setup.title: What this stretch of life looks like
setup.subtitle: This shapes the questions and tips — not a score on who you are.

period.highPressure: Extra pressure at work or study
period.routine: Normal routine, with ups and downs
period.transition: A time of change and transitions

fatigue.wornDown: Feeling run down for a while

focus.seekingQuiet: Looking for a bit of calm and balance

insights.dim-stressBalance-high: You break pressure into small pieces instead of letting it run away. That's real resilience.
insights.dim-stressBalance-low: Pressure is taking a big share. One small rule — one task at a time — can turn down the noise.
insights.dim-restEnergy-high: You know how to recharge. Keep that, especially on busy days.
insights.dim-restEnergy-low: Energy is lower than your head demands. A short, intentional break beats a long to-do list.
insights.dim-personalSpace-high: You have a soft but clear boundary. It protects calm without cutting people off.
insights.dim-personalSpace-low: It's easy to give up personal space to please others. Half an hour that's yours isn't a luxury.
insights.overall-strong: Overall you navigate load like a grown-up: with care, without crashing on every wave.
insights.overall-steady: A good human place — clear strengths and a few habits worth strengthening.
insights.overall-developing: There's awareness, but load still leads. A small step beats a perfect plan.
insights.overall-needs-care: Body and mind are asking for relief. That's not failure — it's a signal to pause a little.
insights.period-highPressure: In a high-pressure stretch, boundaries wear down fast. Cut what you can, even if it's just one task.
insights.period-routine: In routine it's easy to ignore small tiredness until it grows. Check your energy midweek.
insights.period-transition: Transitions drain energy even when they're positive. Give yourself time to adjust without rushing.
insights.fatigue-rested: You have a good energy base — use it wisely, not until empty.
insights.fatigue-midweek: Midweek tiredness is normal. An earlier lights-out tonight beats another coffee.
insights.fatigue-wornDown: Running on empty asks for less push, not more. Ask for help with one thing this week.
insights.focus-timePressure: Time pressure feeds hurry. Stop ten minutes to plan — it saves an hour of mess.
insights.focus-futureWorry: Future worries steal the present. Write three worries on paper — then return to what you can do today.
insights.focus-taskPile: A pile of tasks feels like a mountain. Pick only three for today and let the rest wait.
insights.focus-seekingQuiet: Looking for quiet is a healthy sign. Protect it like an important meeting.

tips.tip-ten-minute-box: Ten-minute box: set a timer, handle one thing only, then stop to breathe.
tips.tip-write-three-worries: Write three worries on paper. What you can do today — mark it. The rest waits for tomorrow.
tips.tip-one-task-rule: One-task rule: until the current one is done — no new tab or list.
tips.tip-earlier-lights-out: Lights out twenty minutes earlier this week — no phone in bed.
tips.tip-short-walk: A ten-minute walk without headphones. Moving your body moves your head too.
tips.tip-water-and-sit: A glass of water and five minutes sitting without a screen — before you go back to the list.
tips.tip-protect-half-hour: Half an hour this week blocked for you in the calendar — like a meeting you can't cancel.
tips.tip-soft-no-script: One line for a gentle no: "My week is full — let's talk next week."
tips.tip-phone-away-meal: One meal a day with no phone on the table.
tips.tip-evening-close: End-of-day ritual: three things you did, one for tomorrow, and phone away from bed.
tips.tip-ask-one-favor: Ask for help with one small thing this week — an errand, a task, or a quiet hour at home.
tips.tip-tiny-joy-today: Plan a tiny joy for today: good coffee, a favorite song, or five minutes in the sun.
